scope_note: Corrective metric-specific synthesis for TierPoint Charlotte Center Park (CL4). Two independent staffing-equivalent sensitivities translate facility-specific continuous NOC and security coverage statements into the FTE capacity needed to cover one simultaneous post; neither is an observed employee count, the functions are not summed, and employer, overlap, shift, absence, residence and payroll remain unknown. A separate opening-configuration electricity sensitivity annualizes the directly reported 1.215 MW usable UPS capacity across utilization and PUE scenarios while checking the source-reported 3,000 kVA service capacity under power-factor assumptions. It is a theoretical nameplate envelope, not metered use, a true-value bound or an economic contribution. No model is created from 530 tons of cooling because electrical demand would require unobserved COP, part-load, redundancy and operating-hour inputs, and no model is created from generator counts, unit ratings, runtime or fuel storage because emergency standby nameplates do not measure annual operation.

estimates.label: Minimum staffing-equivalent capacity for one continuously covered NOC post

period.label: Annualized staffing-equivalent sensitivity anchored to the March 2014 opening statement

scope.label: One simultaneous onsite NOC coverage post at Windstream Charlotte Four / TierPoint CL4

interval.interpretation: Low, central and high apply 0%, 15% and 30% relief factors to the theoretical 8,760 annual coverage hours divided by 2,080 paid hours per FTE. This is the staffing capacity for one simultaneous post, not an observed employee-count interval.

parameters.name: continuous_coverage_hours

provenance.detail: The opening release says the onsite NOC was fully staffed 24 x 7 x 365

parameters.transformation: Annual hours requiring coverage by at least one assumed simultaneous post

parameters.name: paid_hours_per_fte

provenance.detail: Forty paid hours per week for 52 weeks before relief coverage

parameters.transformation: Divides annual coverage hours into theoretical FTE capacity

parameters.name: low_relief_factor

provenance.detail: No vacation, holiday, illness, training, turnover or schedule-overlap allowance

parameters.transformation: Low endpoint and strict mathematical floor

provenance.detail: Fifteen percent allowance for leave, absence, training and shift overlap
Thirty percent allowance for leave, absence, training, turnover and shift overlap

estimates.confidence_rationale: Continuous facility-specific NOC coverage is directly stated, but one simultaneous post, paid hours and all relief factors are assumptions; actual staffing could be materially higher and could include remote or contracted support.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a reproducible minimum staffing-capacity scale for a continuously occupied operating function without inventing actual CL4 headcount or payroll.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Simultaneous NOC posts by shift, filled employee and contractor headcount, employer, paid hours, leave and absence coverage, annual-average FTE, occupations, wages, payroll and residence

derivation.formula: 8,760 continuous coverage hours ÷ 2,080 paid hours per FTE × relief factor
assumptions: The phrase fully staffed 24 x 7 x 365 implies at least one simultaneous onsite NOC coverage post.
One FTE supplies 2,080 paid hours before relief coverage.
Relief factors of 1.00, 1.15 and 1.30 bracket scheduling, leave and absence sensitivity.

limitations: The source does not report an employee count or number of simultaneous NOC posts.
The model is a staffing-equivalent requirement, not proof that the positions were filled by distinct employees or Mecklenburg residents.
No wage or payroll is inferred.
The separate current security sensitivity is not added because staffing overlap and contracting are unresolved.
estimates.notes: Minimum one-post coverage sensitivity only; not a reported job, FTE, payroll or causal contribution.

estimates.label: Opening-configuration theoretical annual electricity sensitivity

period.label: Full-year theoretical sensitivity using the March 2014 opening configuration; not calendar-2014 use

scope.label: Windstream Charlotte Four / TierPoint CL4 opening-day 1.215 MW usable UPS configuration

interval.interpretation: Low, central and high pair 25%, 50% and 75% IT-load utilization with PUE 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6. Each endpoint is checked against the 3,000 kVA service capacity at assumed power factors of 0.8, 0.9 and 1.0; the service ceiling does not bind. This is not actual use or a true-value bound.

parameters.name: usable_ups_capacity

provenance.detail: Opening-day usable UPS capacity

parameters.transformation: Converted to kW and multiplied by hours, utilization and PUE

parameters.name: utility_service_capacity

provenance.detail: Opening release's first-day utility capacity

parameters.transformation: Converted to an assumed real-power ceiling using each power-factor scenario

provenance.detail: Non-leap full-year theoretical annualization

estimates.confidence_rationale: UPS and utility-service nameplates are facility-specific, but utilization, PUE, power factor, redundancy, occupancy and operating hours are not observed and dominate the sensitivity.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a reproducible scale envelope for the opening electrical configuration after direct meter and bill searches were exhausted, while preventing nameplate capacity from being presented as observed consumption.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Interval-metered electricity, utility bills, coincident peak, occupied IT load, facility PUE, power factor, transformer/feed redundancy, renewable procurement, rate impacts and calendar-2014 operating duration

derivation.formula: min(1.215 MW usable UPS × IT utilization × PUE, 3,000 kVA utility service × power factor ÷ 1,000) × 1,000 kW/MW × 8,760 hours
assumptions: IT utilization scenarios are 25%, 50% and 75% of usable UPS capacity.
Power-factor scenarios are 0.8, 0.9 and 1.0 for the 3,000 kVA service-capacity check.
The model annualizes 8,760 hours and is not a claim about partial calendar-year 2014 operation.

limitations: No meter, bill, utilization, site PUE or power factor is public.
The interval is a scenario envelope, not a true lower or upper bound on use.
The March opening means this is not calendar-2014 consumption.
The 3,000 kVA service rating is nonbinding in all displayed scenarios and its feed/redundancy definition is not reported.
The 530-ton cooling nameplate is not converted to electricity because COP, part-load, redundancy and operating hours are unobserved.
No electricity cost, emissions, water use or economic output is inferred.
estimates.notes: Opening-configuration engineering sensitivity only; not actual annual consumption, utility demand or a contribution-account total.
